label: rem:trivial-knot-photon-interpretation
title: Term-by-term interpretation of the trivial knot operator on colored photons
html:
The trivial (identity) operator \mathbf{1} implies a photon pair collision without inserted crossings. Every resulting structure derives strictly from the photons' inherent color content. The 16 cross-terms from the full expansion reduce to normal form via the Hecke and Yang--Baxter relations.

Here "trivial" means the trivial Hecke representation — the identity element \mathbf{1} = T_e \in H_n(R, q), carrying no crossings and no closed strand. It is not the unknot 0_1 = T_{1,0}, which is a closed strand and denotes the neutrino (building-block knots, torus-knot generators). See the photon-vs-unknot rule in notation-collisions.md.

See Table 1. See Table 2. See Table 3. See Table 4. See Table 5.

Vacuum channel (\gamma): Co-polarized photons amplify the vacuum channel. The Hopf dressing \varphi_{01} does not feed the vacuum. Linear polarization channels (\sigma_0, \sigma_1): Receive symmetric additive and Hecke contributions, plus asymmetric twist-rotation terms where Hopf dressing converts into orthogonal polarization. Positive Hopf link (L_+): Fed preferentially because the photon's internal twist is inherently positive (L_+). Negative Hopf link (L_-): Restricted to cross-polarization and Hopf self-products, demonstrating a clear chirality signature. Electron channel (e^-): Opens only when at least one photon carries Hopf dressing, supplying the necessary crossings to form a trefoil.

If all polarizations vanish, \gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2 = \mathbf{1}. L_+ and L_- vanish when photons are co-polarized on a single axis. Electrons cannot emerge from photons lacking twist content. The Hopf link functions as a 90^\circ polarization rotator: combining Hopf dressing with linear polarization absorbs the crossing and emits orthogonal polarization.
